import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Gromov's theorem on groups of polynomial growth

*Reference:*
 - [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gromov%27s_theorem_on_groups_of_polynomial_growth)
-/

/-
Note: this was obtained in work with Kasia Jankiewicz and Catherine Pfaff, and using
Claude 4.0 Sonnet: https://claude.ai/share/918bb269-bd28-4c09-b84e-cab579c836e8
-/

namespace GromovPolynomialGrowth

open Filter

variable {G : Type*} [Group G]

/-- Infinite groups do not satisfy polynomial growth over `ℕ` for any degree `d` because when
`d = 0` this reduces to the unbounded nature of `growthFunction` while `n = 0` works when `d ≠ 0`.
Thus a finitely-generated infinite nilpotent group would be a counter-example to
Gromov's theorem when quantifying over all of `ℕ`, and so `n = 0` should be excluded. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem growthFunction_not_polynomial_of_infinite [Infinite G] {S : Set G} (hS : S.Finite)
    (h : Subgroup.closure S = ⊤) {C : ℝ} (d : ℕ) :
    ∃ (n : ℕ), C * n ^ d < GrowthFunction S n := by
  by_cases hd : d = 0
  · obtain ⟨n, _, hn⟩ := exists_lt_of_tendsto_atTop (tendsto_atTop_growthFunction_of_infinite hS h)
      0 ⌈C⌉₊
    use n
    grw [Nat.le_ceil C]
    simpa [hd] using mod_cast hn
  · exact ⟨0, by simp [hd, growthFunction_zero]⟩

variable (G)

/-- **Gromov's Polynomial Growth Theorem** : A finitely generated group has
    polynomial growth if and only if it is virtually nilpotent. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 20]
theorem GromovPolynomialGrowthTheorem [Group.FG G] :
    HasPolynomialGrowth G ↔ Group.IsVirtuallyNilpotent G := by
  sorry

end GromovPolynomialGrowth

reformulations.difference: HasPolynomialGrowth permits a nonsymmetric finite generating set and uses a bound C*n^d with C > 0 and d : ℕ for every n > 0. Wikipedia describes symmetric generators and an arbitrary polynomial upper bound.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: CayleyBall already permits letters in S and their inverses. Replacing S by S ∪ S⁻¹ preserves every ball and the generated subgroup, and gives a finite symmetric set. A bound C*n^d for positive n gives the polynomial bound p(n) = C*n^d + 1 for all natural n, including n = 0 because the zero-radius ball has cardinality 1. Conversely, for n ≥ 1 and D = p.natDegree, p(n) ≤ (∑_{i≤D} |p.coeff i|)*n^D, so adding 1 to this coefficient sum supplies a positive C. Eventual bounds and bounds for all positive radii are also equivalent by increasing C to cover the finite initial segment. These equivalences are proved in /workspace/review/scratch.lean, including Review.polynomial_iff_symmetric_polynomial_bound and Review.polynomial_iff_eventual.

reformulations.difference: Mathlib defines nilpotence using the upper central series reaching the whole group, whereas Wikipedia uses the lower central series terminating at the identity. Mathlib's FiniteIndex is expressed through a nonzero natural-valued index.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Subgroup.isNilpotent_iff_lowerCentralSeries gives exactly the lower-central-series characterization, and Subgroup.finiteIndex_iff_finite_quotient identifies FiniteIndex with finiteness of the coset space. In particular, infinite index, whose natural-valued default is zero, is excluded. Review.virtually_nilpotent_iff_lower_series proves the resulting existential equivalence in the scratch file. Review.statement_iff_source combines it with the polynomial-growth equivalence to prove an ↔ between the complete formulations, without using the sorry-containing Gromov theorem.

review.notes: Both declarations were checked. The test growthFunction_not_polynomial_of_infinite correctly refutes a monomial bound imposed at every natural radius: n = 0 handles d ≠ 0, and unbounded word-ball cardinalities handle d = 0. It does not assert ¬HasPolynomialGrowth. Finite generating sets guarantee finite nonempty balls, so Set.ncard's infinite-set default cannot affect either declaration. Boundary checks covered empty generating sets, trivial and finite groups, and ℤ with a singleton generator, whose growth at radii 0 and 1 is 1 and 3. /workspace/review/scratch.lean compiles without errors or warnings; its equivalence proofs and the file's existing test have no sorryAx dependencies. The research solved category agrees with the source's record of Gromov's 1981 theorem.
